source.places: US Census Bureau 2025 Gazetteer places (internal points)
source.note: “why” lines are short editorial context; numbers are in each city’s sourced card.

focus.label: Focus
focus.description: Colorado River, California, Upper Basin & Utah

towns.name: St. George
towns.why: One of the fastest-growing U.S. metros, on the Virgin River, a Colorado tributary.

towns.name: Moab
towns.why: Gateway to Arches and Canyonlands, on the Colorado River.

towns.name: Pahrump
towns.why: Las Vegas’s neighbour over the mountains, which runs on groundwater, not the Colorado.

towns.name: Mesquite
towns.why: Virgin River farm town turned retirement and resort city.

towns.name: Cedar City
towns.why: Fast-growing southern Utah city on a closed groundwater basin.

towns.name: Page
towns.why: Built in 1957 to house the workers building Glen Canyon Dam.

towns.name: Grand Junction
towns.why: Where the Gunnison meets the Colorado, at the centre of the Grand Valley’s irrigated orchards.

towns.name: Steamboat Springs
towns.why: Yampa River ski town, a Colorado River tributary in the Upper Basin.

towns.name: Provo
towns.why: Utah Valley city fed partly by Colorado River water carried by the Central Utah Project.

towns.name: Yuma
towns.why: The heart of the U.S. winter-vegetable harvest, irrigated from the Colorado.

towns.name: El Centro
towns.why: Imperial Valley’s county seat, fed by the All-American Canal.

towns.anchorSource: OpenStreetMap city node via Nominatim (Census internal point is offshore: the city boundary includes the Farallon Islands)

towns.name: Salt Lake City
towns.why: Wasatch Front capital, fed mainly by mountain streams and the Provo River system.

towns.name: Denver
towns.why: East of the Continental Divide, but part of its water is tunnelled from the Colorado headwaters.

towns.name: Sacramento
towns.why: At the confluence of the Sacramento and American rivers.

towns.name: San Jose
towns.why: Santa Clara Valley city mixing local reservoirs, groundwater and imported water.

towns.name: Oakland
towns.why: East Bay city supplied from the Mokelumne River by EBMUD.

towns.name: Fresno
towns.why: San Joaquin Valley city that shifted from groundwater toward river water.

towns.name: Albuquerque
towns.why: Rio Grande city that also draws Colorado River water through the San Juan–Chama Project.

towns.name: Santa Fe
towns.why: New Mexico’s capital, also a San Juan–Chama Project user.

towns.name: El Paso
towns.why: Desert city on the Rio Grande known for desalinating brackish groundwater.

towns.name: Colorado Springs
towns.why: Front Range city pumping Colorado headwaters water across the Divide.

towns.name: Fort Collins
towns.why: On the Cache la Poudre, fed in part by the Colorado–Big Thompson Project.

towns.name: Cheyenne
towns.why: Wyoming’s capital, which imports water across the Divide from the Little Snake basin.

towns.name: Ogden
towns.why: Weber River city on the Wasatch Front.

towns.name: Boise
towns.why: Snake River Plain city on the Boise River.

towns.name: Reno
towns.why: On the Truckee River, which runs from Lake Tahoe to Pyramid Lake.
